## Research Question & Motivation

-   What is the general publics interaction with Mathematics?

-   We will examine this question through analysis of page view statistics for Math-related Wikipedia articles

-   Outline:

1.  Overview of data set

2.  Wikipedia page connection graph

3.  Viewership Statistics

4.  Relevant events impacting page views

## Math Wikipedia Dataset

-   Wikipedia Math Essentials from UCI Machine Learning Repository. (<https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/605/wikipedia+math+essentials>)

-   Daily view count data for 1068 Wikipedia pages related to Mathematics and Statistics, over period of 2 years, with one instance per page per day

-   Period in question: March 16, 2019 - March 15, 2021


-   Variables: Page Name, Date, View Count, Edges (number of hyperlinks with other pages)

```{r view of data, echo=FALSE}
setwd("**")
df <- read.csv("MathWikipediaCorrected.csv")
colnames(df)[3] <- 'Edges'
head(df)
```

## Wikipedia Page Connection Map

```{r jiazhe plot, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, error=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#file_path <- "**/wikivital_mathematics.json"


data <- fromJSON('wikivital_mathematics.json')
required_fields <- c("edges", "weights")

g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = data[["edges"]], directed = FALSE)
E(g)$weight <- data[["weights"]]


communities <- cluster_louvain(g, weights = E(g)$weight)
membership <- communities$membership

V(g)$community <- as.factor(membership)


levels(V(g)$community) <- c("Applied Math", "Number Theory", "(Abstract) Algebra",
                             "Geometry", "Calculus (Analysis)", "Logic", "Statistics",
                             "Combinatorics")


g_contract <- contract.vertices(g, membership, vertex.attr.comb = list(name = function(x) x[1]))

layout_contract <- layout_in_circle(g_contract)


global_scaling <- 3   
local_scaling <- 0.3   


global_positions <- lapply(1:nrow(layout_contract), function(i) layout_contract[i,])
names(global_positions) <- sort(unique(membership))


final_layout <- matrix(NA, nrow = vcount(g), ncol = 2)

for (comm in sort(unique(membership))) {

  node_indices <- which(membership == comm)

  subg <- induced_subgraph(g, node_indices)

  local_layout <- layout_with_fr(subg, weights = E(subg)$weight)

  local_layout_centered <- sweep(local_layout, 2, colMeans(local_layout))
 

  offset <- global_positions[[as.character(comm)]] * global_scaling
 

  final_layout[node_indices, ] <- local_layout_centered * local_scaling +
    matrix(offset, nrow = length(node_indices), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
}


node_layout <- create_layout(g, layout = "manual", x = final_layout[,1], y = final_layout[,2])



plot <- ggraph(node_layout) +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = weight, filter = weight >= 4), edge_alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_node_point(aes(color = community), size = 3) +
  scale_edge_width(guide = "none") +
  theme_void()


plot
```

## Top 50 Connected Pages

```{r connections, echo=FALSE}

connection_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(Page) %>%
  summarize(Total_Connections = sum(Edges)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Connections)) %>%
  top_n(50, Total_Connections)

ggplot(connection_summary, aes(x = reorder(Page, -Total_Connections), y = Total_Connections)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "skyblue") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Total Connections per Wikipedia Page",
       x = "Page",
       y = "Number of Connections") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Most Viewed Pages

```{r}
df1 <- df %>%
  group_by(Page) %>%
  summarise(Views = sum(Views)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Views))
df1
```

## Average Number of Views per Weekday

```{r heatmap, echo=FALSE}
suppressWarnings({

heatmap_data <- df %>%
  mutate(Weekday = wday(Date, label = TRUE),
         Month = month(Date, label = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(Weekday, Month) %>%
  summarize(Avg_Views = mean(Views), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = Weekday, y = Month, fill = Avg_Views)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Heatmap of Average Math-Related Wikipedia Page Views",
       x = "Day of Week",
       y = "Month",
       fill = "Average Number of Views")
})
```

## Math Wikipedia and Media

-   Question: What types of events influence public interests in Mathematics, and can we quantify this through Wikipedia page views?
-   What do the sources of these sparks in interest tell us about the best way to promote Mathematics to a wider audience?
-   Three cases: Math related holidays, mainstream press stories, and Youtube videos

## Shiny App

<https://mlewispeinad.shinyapps.io/project1/>

-   Allows us to filter through different Math Wikipedia pages and date ranges

## Case 1: Math Holidays

-   Two notable Math holidays

-   Pi Day (March 14)

-   Fibonacci Day (November 23)

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
![](https://i.redd.it/dd2w9bqh5o4b1.png){width="400"}
:::

## Case 2: Mainstream Media Articles

-   From examining archived articles from publications such as the New York Times, Math related articles are few and far between in the mainstream press.
-   Common type of Math-related news article: Obituaries for famous Mathematicians
-   Example: John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020), known for his contributions to both academic and recreational Mathematics, for example Coding Theory

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
![](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/images/ic/320x320/p08b9bd6.jpg){width="200"}
:::

## Exponential Growth

-   Early during the COVID pandemic, many people were curious about how the virus was spreading so quickly, leading to talk about the Mathematics behind 'Exponential Growth'.

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
![](images/expog.png){width="500"}
:::

## Case 3: Youtube

-   Youtube has served as a thriving community for exposing Mathematics to a general audience
-   Example: 3Blue1Brown (Grant Sanderson), known for producing accessible videos on advanced topics in Math and Science with slick animations
-   7 Million subscribers as of 2025

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
![](data:image/png;base64,){alt="3Blue1Brown | Knot Theory Tie – DFTBA" width="298"}

![](https://mathematics.stanford.edu/sites/mathematics/files/styles/hs_medium_square_360x360/public/media/image/sanderson_grant_0.png?h=8cd830a5&itok=sboDiPUH){alt="Stanford Math Alumnus, Grant Sanderson, to Receive Communications Award  from AMS | Mathematics" width="200"}
:::

## Conclusion

-   Given the prevalence of Wikipedia in many of our everyday lives, we can learn a lot about societies relationship with Mathematics through examining trends on Wikipedia
-   An important takeaway is that alternative media outlets, such Youtube, are more effective at promoting interest in Mathematics than the traditional press
-   Happy early Pi Day!
